title: Reading a Paper Efficiently and Spotting Spin and Hype

hook.en: Nobody reads a paper from the first word to the last. Experts read in a smart order, and they notice when the words in the abstract promise more than the numbers deliver. That gap is called spin.
hook.ur: Koi paper pehle lafz se aakhri tak nahi parhta. Maahir samajhdar tarteeb mein parhte hain, aur woh dekhte hain jab abstract ke alfaaz numbers se zyada waade karte hain. Is farq ko spin kehte hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll read a paper in three passes, know where to look for the answer to your question, spot common types of spin, and separate a press headline from what the study actually showed.
goal.ur: End tak aap paper teen pass mein parhenge, jaanenge ke apne sawal ka jawab kahan dekhna hai, spin ki aam qismein pehchanenge, aur press ke sar-khat ko us se alag karenge jo study ne asal mein dikhaya.

text.en: Read **in three passes**. Pass one (two minutes): title, abstract, the last paragraph of the introduction and the conclusion. Do I care? Pass two (eight minutes): the methods and the main results table and figure. Can I trust it, and how big is the effect? Pass three (only if needed): the details, limitations and references. **Spin** is reporting that makes a treatment look better than the results show, for example calling a non-significant result a trend or highlighting a small outcome.
text.ur: **Teen pass** mein parhein. Pehla pass (do minute): title, abstract, introduction ka aakhri paragraph aur conclusion. Kya mujhe dilchaspi hai? Doosra pass (aath minute): methods aur main results ki table aur figure. Kya bharosa kar sakta hoon, aur asar kitna bara hai? Teesra pass (sirf zaroorat ho to): tafseelat, kamzoriyan aur hawale. **Spin** woh report hai jo ilaaj ko nateejon se behtar dikhati hai, masalan ghair-significant nateeje ko rujhan kehna ya chhote outcome ko numaya karna.

text.en: Think of a **property advertisement**. It says "sunny, spacious, near the market". The visit tells you the house faces a wall, the rooms are small and the market is a fifteen-minute drive. The abstract is the advertisement; the results table is the visit. Always go and look.
text.ur: **Jaidad ka ishtihaar** sochein. Kehta hai "roshan, kushada, bazaar ke qareeb". Dekhne jayein to ghar deewar ki taraf hai, kamray chhote hain aur bazaar pandrah minute door. Abstract ishtihaar hai; results table daura hai. Hamesha jaa kar dekhein.

title.en: Common types of spin and how to spot them
title.ur: Spin ki aam qismein aur unhein kaise pehchanein

rows.en: "A trend towards improvement" when p is above 0.05
rows.ur: "Behtari ki taraf rujhan" jab p 0.05 se oopar ho

rows.en: Look at the confidence interval: does it include no effect?
rows.ur: Confidence interval dekhein: kya is mein koi asar na hona shamil hai?

rows.en: The primary outcome failed, but a different one is highlighted
rows.ur: Primary outcome nakam raha, lekin doosra numaya kiya gaya

rows.en: Compare with the registered primary outcome
"Pain fell in the treatment group" with no comparison to controls
rows.ur: "Ilaaj group mein dard kam hua" control se muqabla kiye baghair

rows.en: The between-group difference is what matters
rows.ur: Groups ke beech ka farq ahem hai

rows.en: "Worked in women under 40" after the whole trial was null
rows.ur: "40 se kam khawateen mein kaam kiya" jab poora trial null tha

rows.en: Was the subgroup planned in advance?
rows.ur: Kya subgroup pehle se tay tha?

rows.en: Ask for the absolute difference: 2 in 100 to 1 in 100 is a 50 percent drop of 1 person
rows.ur: Absolute farq poochhein: 100 mein 2 se 1 par aana 50 fisad kami hai, 1 shakhs ki

question.en: A trial's abstract says "the treatment group showed a promising trend towards less pain (p = 0.11)". What does this most likely mean?
question.ur: Trial ka abstract kehta hai "ilaaj group mein dard mein kami ka ummeed afza rujhan (p = 0.11)". Iska zyada imkaan kya matlab hai?

feedback.en: The result did not reach significance.

text.en: The difference was not statistically significant, and the wording is spin; look at the confidence interval and the primary outcome
text.ur: Farq shumariyati taur par significant nahi tha, aur alfaaz spin hain; confidence interval aur primary outcome dekhein

feedback.en: Yes — "promising trend" is a common way to dress up a null result.
feedback.ur: Haan — "ummeed afza rujhan" null nateeje ko sajane ka aam tareeqa hai.

question.en: A headline reads "New exercise cuts injury risk by 50 percent". In the paper, injuries fell from 2 in 100 to 1 in 100. How should you describe this to a coach?
question.ur: Sar-khat hai "Nayi exercise se chot ka khatra 50 fisad kam". Paper mein chotein 100 mein 2 se 1 par aayi. Coach ko kaise bayan karenge?

text.en: Fifty percent of athletes will avoid injury
text.ur: 50 fisad athletes chot se bach jayenge

feedback.en: The headline does not mean that.

text.en: Half of all injuries are prevented
text.ur: Aadhi chotein rok di jati hain

feedback.ur: Yeh relative kami ko ghalat parhna hai.

text.en: The risk fell by one percentage point, so about 100 athletes need to do it for one fewer injury
text.ur: Khatra ek fisad point kam hua, yani takreeban 100 athletes ke karne par ek chot kam

feedback.en: Yes — the absolute change shows the real size; the relative number sounds bigger.
feedback.ur: Haan — absolute tabdeeli asal size batati hai; relative number bara sunayi deta hai.

question.en: In which order is it usually best to read a paper?
question.ur: Paper parhne ki aam taur par behtareen tarteeb kya hai?

text.en: Start at the introduction and read word for word
text.ur: Introduction se shuru kar ke lafz ba lafz parhein

feedback.en: That wastes time on papers you will not use.
feedback.ur: Is se un papers par waqt zaya hota hai jo istemal nahi honge.

text.en: Abstract and conclusion, then methods and results, then details only if you need them
text.ur: Abstract aur conclusion, phir methods aur results, phir tafseelat sirf zaroorat par

feedback.en: Yes — a three-pass approach saves time and exposes spin.
feedback.ur: Haan — teen pass ka tareeqa waqt bachata hai aur spin ko ujagar karta hai.

feedback.en: The conclusion is where spin lives.
feedback.ur: Conclusion mein hi spin hota hai.

text.en: **Believing the abstract and the headline.** Authors, journals and press offices all have reasons to make results sound exciting. Spin is not always dishonest; it can be wishful thinking. The fix is simple habit: after reading the conclusion, find the primary outcome, the between-group difference and its confidence interval, and ask whether the conclusion matches them.
text.ur: **Abstract aur sar-khat par yaqeen karna.** Musannifon, journals aur press offices sab ke paas nateeje dilchasp banane ki wajuhaat hoti hain. Spin hamesha be-imani nahi hota; yeh khwahish-mand soch bhi ho sakti hai. Hal saada aadat hai: conclusion parhne ke baad primary outcome, groups ke beech farq aur uska confidence interval dhoondein, aur poochhein ke conclusion in se milta hai ya nahi.

text.en: **Translate headlines for patients.** If a patient shows you a news story, say: "Let us look at what the study actually measured. How many people, compared with what, and how big was the change?" This keeps you friendly and curious instead of dismissive, and teaches patients to ask the same questions.
text.ur: **Sar-khat mareezon ke liye tarjuma karein.** Agar mareez khabar dikhaye to kahein: "Dekhte hain study ne asal mein kya naapa. Kitne log, kis se muqabla, aur tabdeeli kitni badi thi?" Isse aap dostana aur tajassus bhare rehte hain, bajaye radd karne ke, aur mareez wohi sawal poochhna seekhte hain.

question.en: Why are positive results more likely to get a press release?
question.ur: Musbat nateejon ke liye press release ka zyada imkaan kyun?

answer.en: Journals, funders and news outlets prefer clear, positive and exciting findings. Studies with null results are less often published (publication bias) and less often written about. That is why the news and even the literature can look more optimistic than the truth, and why systematic reviews that look for unpublished work are important.
answer.ur: Journals, funders aur khabar ke idare saaf, musbat aur dilchasp nateeje pasand karte hain. Null nateejon wali studies kam shaya hoti hain (publication bias) aur un par kam likha jata hai. Isi liye khabrein aur literature bhi haqeeqat se zyada ummeed afza lag sakte hain, aur isi liye woh systematic reviews ahem hain jo ghair-shaya kaam dhoondte hain.

beats.patient: A news article says "Foam rolling boosts performance, study finds." You find the study: 20 students, no control group, and the "boost" was a 1 percent change in sprint time that was not significant.
beats.assessment: The headline reports a within-group trend as proof, and the study has no control and is too small.
beats.treatment: Ignore the headline, read the methods and results, and tell the client the result is interesting but too small and uncontrolled to rely on.
beats.reassess: You keep foam rolling as an optional comfort tool and do not promise a performance gain.

text.en: **Do not let hype change a safe plan.** A catchy headline about a risky technique, an unregulated supplement or a very intense programme should not make you drop what is safe and proven. If a patient wants to try something based on a headline, check the safety and explain the evidence before agreeing.
text.ur: **Hype se mehfooz plan na badlein.** Khatarnak technique, ghair-munazzam supplement ya bohat shiddat wali programme ke baare mein dilkash sar-khat aap ko mehfooz aur sabit shuda cheez chhorne par majboor na kare. Agar mareez sar-khat ki bunyad par kuch aazmana chahe to razamandi se pehle safety jaanchein aur evidence samjhayein.

text.en: A study of randomised trials with statistically non-significant primary outcomes found that spin, meaning reporting that distracts from the null result, was common in the abstracts and conclusions: about 40 percent of reports had spin in the abstract, and it was often a focus on secondary outcomes or on within-group changes. Greenhalgh's guide to reading papers recommends first working out what kind of paper it is and what question it addresses, before judging detail.
text.ur: Statistically non-significant primary outcome wale randomised trials ki ek study mein paya gaya ke spin, yani aisi report jo null nateeje se tawajjo hata de, abstracts aur conclusions mein aam thi: takreeban 40 fisad reports ke abstract mein spin tha, aur aksar secondary outcomes ya group ke andar ki tabdeeliyon par zor tha. Greenhalgh ki papers parhne ki rehnumai tajweez karti hai ke tafseel jaanchne se pehle pehle jaanein ke paper kis qism ka hai aur kis sawal ka jawab deta hai.

text.en: **Three passes, Primary outcome, Between groups, Absolute numbers.** Read in three passes, find the primary outcome, compare between groups and ask for absolute numbers.
text.ur: **Teen pass, Primary outcome, Groups ke beech, Absolute numbers.** Teen pass mein parhein, primary outcome dhoondein, groups ke beech muqabla karein aur absolute numbers poochhein.

summary.en: Read in three passes: abstract and conclusion, methods and results, then details.
summary.ur: Teen pass mein parhein: abstract aur conclusion, methods aur results, phir tafseelat.

summary.en: Spin makes results sound better than they are: trends, secondary outcomes, within-group changes, subgroup fishing and relative numbers.
summary.ur: Spin nateejon ko haqeeqat se behtar sunata hai: rujhan, secondary outcomes, group ke andar tabdeeliyan, subgroup fishing aur relative numbers.

summary.en: Check the primary outcome, the between-group difference and absolute numbers before believing a headline.
summary.ur: Sar-khat par yaqeen se pehle primary outcome, groups ke beech farq aur absolute numbers dekhein.

back.en: Reporting that makes a treatment look better than the results show.
back.ur: Aisi report jo ilaaj ko nateejon se behtar dikhaye.

back.en: Positive results are more likely to be published than null ones.
back.ur: Musbat nateeje null se zyada shaya hote hain.

back.en: Relative changes sound large even when the real difference is small.
back.ur: Relative tabdeeliyan bari sunayi deti hain jab asal farq chhota ho.

front.en: What are the three reading passes?
front.ur: Parhne ke teen pass kaun se hain?

back.en: Abstract and conclusion; methods and results; details if needed.
back.ur: Abstract aur conclusion; methods aur results; zaroorat par tafseelat.
